lab.title: Lab Challenges
lab.subtitle: Behold, the mighty botnets!
lab.description: This year's CTF theme focuses on botnet development, challenging participants to explore how botnets are designed, built, and operated in a controlled environment. By understanding the inner workings of botnets, their communication mechanisms, and attack strategies, participants will gain valuable insights into how these threats function in the real world. The ultimate goal is to bridge offensive and defensive security knowledge, equipping defenders with the skills and understanding needed to better detect, analyze, mitigate, and defend against botnet threats.

questions.title: Botnet Challenge
questions.description:
Participants are challenged to develop and deploy a botnet inspired by existing botnets such as Mirai or Satori. The botnet should demonstrate key characteristics of real-world botnet architectures, including command-and-control (C2) communication, device management, and coordinated operations.

Participants may use publicly disclosed CVEs to demonstrate how vulnerable systems can be compromised within the designated CTF environment. The objective is to understand how botnets are constructed and operate, providing defensive teams with a realistic adversarial scenario to investigate and defend against.

Once development is complete, the submitted botnet will be examined by the referees and defensive teams, who will evaluate its behavior, architecture, and security implications.
